red_interpretation: The red mark is a narrow inverted-V at exact center-back: the two pressed fold edges of one inverted pleat. The folds face toward each other, their edges butting together at a single apex point caught in the yoke seam, then separating by only ~1.5-2 cm as they descend ~5-6 cm before releasing into fullness. They are construction fold lines to be rendered as real creased folds in white fabric — not contrast fabric, not stitched red lines.
geometry_summary: Standard dress-shirt back with a straight horizontal yoke seam across the full back width (drawn as one dashed topstitch line, seam at y≈48 of 191px). At the exact horizontal center of the back (x≈98-99, body spans ~x50-148), one inverted pleat is set into the yoke seam: two mirror-image folds whose pressed edges converge to a single apex ON the yoke seam and diverge downward ~3px (≈1/30 of back width, ~1.5-2 cm real scale) over an ~11px drop — about 8% (≈1/12) of the 136px yoke-to-hem length, i.e. the visible converging fold edges extend only ~5-6 cm below the yoke before blending into soft released fullness. No darts, no other pleats; the lower back is a plain uninterrupted panel to a curved stitched shirttail hem. Long sleeves with gauntlet plackets and single-button cuffs, dashed stitching along armholes, cuffs, and hem as standard. Contrast with siblings: Center Pleats draws two PARALLEL fold edges ~8px (~4 cm) apart below the yoke (outward-facing box-pleat reading); Box Pleat to Bottom runs its center fold lines the full length y48→184 to the hem; Side Pleat places short pleat marks near the yoke ends (x≈60, x≈132); Double Darts has curved dart seams at mid-back and no pleat.
counts: Pleats: 1 inverted center-back pleat formed by 2 converging folds (2 red fold edges total). Darts: 0. Yoke seams: 1 straight horizontal seam, full width, drawn with a single dashed topstitch row. Other seams as standard in drawing: 2 armhole seams, 2 side seams, 1 curved stitched hem, sleeve plackets and cuff seams. No seams or stitch lines below the yoke other than side seams and hem.
